provenance.compiled_from: Caprolactam, the nylon-6 monomer: a background ion of open-air ionization, present in the air and system blanks of an ambient (DART) source, where the ion at m/z 114.09194 is read as caprolactam from nylon residues or airborne laboratory background (Narcelli Pestana de Aguiar et al. 2026, the section on background contributions); and a compound of indoor air, C6H11NO detected protonated in the water-soluble gases of 7 of 13 homes (Duncan et al. 2019, Table 2). Formula checked against PubChem.
provenance.caveat: Both works assign the formula, not the structure: the first calls the ion caprolactam-like. Mascope's demo uronium spectra hold caprolactam's urea adduct, C7H16N3O2+ at m/z 174.1237, in every file of one instrument, which is why the list anchors the uronium chemistry's calibrants.
